export function getSectionColor(sectionId) {
  return SECTION_COLORS[(sectionId - 1) % SECTION_COLORS.length];
}

export function shuffle(arr) {
  const a = [...arr];
  for (let i = a.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
    [a[i], a[j]] = [a[j], a[i]];
  }
  return a;
}

export function getQuestionsBySection(sectionIds) {
  // empty array = all sections
  if (!sectionIds || sectionIds.length === 0) {
    return OEC_DATA.flatMap(s => s.questions);
  }
  return OEC_DATA
    .filter(s => sectionIds.includes(s.id))
    .flatMap(s => s.questions);
}

const OEC_DATA = [
  {
    id: 1,
    name: "History & Legal",
    questionCount: 21,
    questions: [
      { num: 1, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "The course called \"Outdoor Emergency Care\" was created by the National Ski Patrol to:", choices: { A: "create a standard of care for ski patrollers and others involved in outdoor emergency care.", B: "provide a standard of training for OEC technicians and others involved in outdoor recreation.", C: "respond to a request from Minnie Dole to develop training for patrollers working at ski resorts.", D: "create a worldwide standard of care for anyone providing outdoor emergency care." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 2, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "The person who first organized a volunteer \"ski patrol\" and then was asked to organize a national patrol was:", choices: { A: "Roger Langely.", B: "Roland Palmedo.", C: "Minnie Dole.", D: "Warren Bowman." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 3, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "The 10th Mountain Division was founded:", choices: { A: "through a request from the U.S. president to Minnie Dole.", B: "after Minnie Dole convinced the U.S. Army that a winter warfare unit would be valuable.", C: "by members of the 87th Mountain Infantry Regiment, many of whom were skiers.", D: "through the Norwegian Army, which had a coldweather unit during World War I." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 4, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "The first emergency responder textbook created exclusively for ski patrollers was titled:", choices: { A: "Winter Emergency Care.", B: "Outdoor Emergency Care.", C: "Ski Safety and First Aid.", D: "Safety on the Snow." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 5, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "Dr. Warren Bowman is considered the father of Outdoor Emergency Care because he:", choices: { A: "was the first program director for the National Ski Patrol.", B: "co-authored the first ski patrol manual with the American Red Cross.", C: "founded the National Ski Patrol as a separate entity.", D: "created the concept of \"intermediate\" medical care for ski patrollers." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 6, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "The 6th Edition of Outdoor Emergency Care:", choices: { A: "must be learned in its entirety through the book and online learning before taking the OEC technician evaluation.", B: "contains the baseline knowledge and skills identified by the U.S. Department of Transportation curriculum for EMTs in all settings.", C: "contains the knowledge and skills identified by the NHSTA for Emergency Medical Responder training plus additional information and training for patrollers.", D: "can only be taught in the winter so that students can practice the skills taught in the course." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 7, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "In order to maintain OEC certification, you must:", choices: { A: "complete the assigned refresher course each year that covers one-third of the curriculum every year during the three year refresher cycle.", B: "complete a refresher course that covers the key objectives of the entire curriculum every year.", C: "complete a refresher course that covers the key objectives of the entire curriculum every three years.", D: "demonstrate CPR and AED skills every two years." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 8, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "Good Samaritan laws generally:", choices: { A: "protect a ski patroller from being sued in every circumstance.", B: "may apply to people who do not receive compensation for helping people.", C: "are the same in every state.", D: "provide enough protection so that you need not to know whether your mountain has insurance." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 9, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "Although regulations may differ from state to state, the general laws that may protect OEC technicians from liability while providing emergency care to a patient are known as:", choices: { A: "emergency rescue protection laws.", B: "Good Samaritan laws.", C: "volunteer rescue liability laws.", D: "first rescuer liability laws." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 10, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "You have just finished your shift, and while driving home still wearing your patrol jacket, you come upon a car collision in which people appear to be injured. You recognize that if you approach the collision wearing your patrol jacket, members of the public may have a reasonable expectation that you will provide care. This expectation is known as:", choices: { A: "the absence of negligence.", B: "professional ethics.", C: "moral obligation.", D: "the doctrine of public reliance." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 11, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "While you are alone and caring for an injured skier in the aid room, a fellow patroller calls and tells you that your own young child was just injured in the terrain park. Concerned for your child, you leave the patient's care unfinished and run to the terrain park. Your action could be viewed as:", choices: { A: "a breach of ethics.", B: "your duty to act.", C: "denial of care.", D: "abandonment." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 12, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "The harming of an individual by not performing up to the technician's standard of training is called:", choices: { A: "negligence.", B: "assault.", C: "gross negligence.", D: "standard of care breach." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 13, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "A situation in which an OEC technician leaves a patient before the patient's care is transferred to another qualified individual is considered:", choices: { A: "negligence.", B: "breach of duty.", C: "abandonment.", D: "assault." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 14, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "You are skiing down your favorite slope and notice a small group gathered around a middleaged man sitting on the ground. You note that the boarder is holding his wrist and appears in pain. He agrees to have you examine him but then refuses any more help. You explain the possible consequences of not splinting the wrist and of the boarder trying to get down the mountain without help. This explanation of the risk of refusing care is provided in order to:", choices: { A: "demonstrate that you know how to treat a wrist injury.", B: "diminish your risk of being accused of abandonment.", C: "reduce your risk of an accusation of battery.", D: "help the patient understand why you are about to put the splint on anyway." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 15, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "Which of the following statements concerning \"standard of training\" is true?", choices: { A: "Acting within the \"standard of training\" is fundamental to reducing an OEC technician's legal risk.", B: "\"Standard of training\" is the same thing as \"standard of care.\"", C: "\"Standard of training\" includes the mountain area's protocols.", D: "\"Standard of training\" includes your state's laws and procedures." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 16, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "Which of the following is not considered a form of patient consent?", choices: { A: "Informed consent", B: "Minor consent", C: "Implied consent", D: "Absolute consent" }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 17, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "Upon finding an unconscious patient at the scene of a bad accident, your next step should be to:", choices: { A: "assume \"implied consent\" and begin to examine and treat the patient.", B: "delay your examination and ask other patrollers to respond as witnesses.", C: "delay your examination until you can locate a spouse or a friend of the patient.", D: "begin your assessment but not provide any treatment until another patroller arrives." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 18, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "The type of consent that is based on an appreciation and understanding of the facts, implications, and possible future consequences of an action is known as:", choices: { A: "implied consent.", B: "educated consent.", C: "expressed consent.", D: "informed consent." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 19, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "Which of the following descriptions is the best example of expressed consent?", choices: { A: "A 37-year-old man who is found unresponsive", B: "A 52-year- old skier who comes to the aid room and asks for help", C: "A 19-year-old male who appears to be intoxicated and lets you examine him", D: "A man who asks you to help his unresponsive 29- year- old diabetic wife" }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 20, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "What type of consent would apply for an unresponsive 28-year-old male victim of a motorcycle collision?", choices: { A: "Expressed consent", B: "Implied consent", C: "Informed consent", D: "Assumed consent" }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 21, sectionId: 1, sectionName: "History & Legal", text: "You arrive at the scene of an accident where a 22-year-old female skier has hit a tree and has a large bleeding cut on her head. When you ask her if she needs help, she refuses care and says she just needs to sit for a while. Noticing the amount of bleeding, you calmly express your concern for her, but she continues to say she doesn't want help. You hesitate to touch her because you are concerned that if you do, she could accuse you of:", choices: { A: "assault.", B: "battery.", C: "breach of duty.", D: "duty to act." }, answer: "B" },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: 2,
    name: "EMS Systems",
    questionCount: 14,
    questions: [
      { num: 1, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "A network of specially trained personnel, equipment, facilities, and other resources that respond to medical emergencies—regardless of cause, location, or the patient's ability to pay—best describes:", choices: { A: "a community wellness program.", B: "a health care system.", C: "an emergency care system.", D: "a public health system." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 2, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Which of the following levels of emergency personnel emphasizes the provision of immediate lifesaving treatment and stabilization to critically ill or injured patients while waiting for additional emergency response?", choices: { A: "Emergency medical technician", B: "Emergency medical responder", C: "Advanced emergency medical technician", D: "Critical care responder" }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 3, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "An OEC technician meets or exceeds the NHTSA national training requirements of:", choices: { A: "an emergency medical technician.", B: "an advanced emergency medical technician.", C: "a paramedic.", D: "an emergency medical responder." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 4, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Most emergency care systems deploy personnel to emergencies using a stratified approach based on the patient's condition or anticipated needs. Which of the following lists presents the normal order of deployment of responders?", choices: { A: "EMT, AEMT, EMR, paramedic", B: "EMR, AEMT, paramedic, EMT", C: "EMR, EMT, AEMT, paramedic", D: "AEMT, paramedic, EMT, EMR" }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 5, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Which of the following is not one of the four nationally recognized prehospital emergency care provider levels?", choices: { A: "Emergency medical technician", B: "Advanced emergency medical technician", C: "Outdoor emergency care technician", D: "Emergency medical responder" }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 6, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Many emergency care systems deploy personnel to emergencies using a tiered approach. OEC technicians are most likely deployed in which tier?", choices: { A: "Tier 1", B: "Tier 2", C: "Tier 3", D: "Tier 4" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 7, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Critical care providers who bring advanced life support equipment, therapies, and interventions to the scene are typically deployed in what tier?", choices: { A: "Tier 1", B: "Tier 2", C: "Tier 3", D: "Tier 4" }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 8, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "The seamless delivery of high-quality emergency medical care as patient transitions from initial contact with an EMT through definitive treatment best describes:", choices: { A: "medical direction.", B: "continuity of care.", C: "integration of health services.", D: "online medical control." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 9, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Which of the following choices is not an example of direct medical oversight?", choices: { A: "Telephone communication", B: "Physical presence of a physician", C: "Written protocols", D: "Video conferencing" }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 10, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Which of the following characteristics is not a characteristic of indirect medical control?", choices: { A: "Communication by radio", B: "Use for expediting patient care", C: "Common use for \"preauthorizing\" routine and life-saving procedures", D: "Provision through the use of protocols" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 11, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Guidelines developed at the local level by emergency personnel familiar with an area's medical needs, available resources, system capabilities, and local standard of care are:", choices: { A: "protocols.", B: "policies.", C: "advanced procedures.", D: "medical attributes." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 12, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Written instructions that indicate what should be done in a given situation are best described as:", choices: { A: "regulations.", B: "protocols.", C: "indirect medical oversight.", D: "direct medical oversight." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 13, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "The reason it is important that OEC technicians participate in quality improvement programs in services in which they work or volunteer is:", choices: { A: "to guarantee that the public receives quality emergency medical care.", B: "to identify changes that, if needed, will ensure the future care a patient receives in is accordance with local protocols and guidelines.", C: "to ensure that individuals making false calls for help are prosecuted.", D: "to identify problem employees and create a corrective action plan for them." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 14, sectionId: 2, sectionName: "EMS Systems", text: "Which of the following methods is the best method for ensuring that the treatment rendered by OEC technicians meets or exceeds customer expectations and national education standards for emergency medical personnel?", choices: { A: "Public education", B: "Prevention training", C: "Continuity of care", D: "Quality improvement" }, answer: "D" },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: 3,
    name: "Rescuer Safety",
    questionCount: 12,
    questions: [
      { num: 1, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "Sometimes the most important thing in a rescue situation is to:", choices: { A: "hydrate injured patients.", B: "take care of yourself.", C: "contact local government.", D: "check vehicle fuel levels." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 2, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "Mental preparedness comes best if you:", choices: { A: "have a negative attitude to prepare for worst cases.", B: "have a neutral attitude to remain calm.", C: "have expectations of difficulties.", D: "have a positive attitude to help deal with difficulties." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 3, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "During a very strenuous rescue, you may need to eat:", choices: { A: "hourly.", B: "when you feel dizzy.", C: "only when feeling hungry.", D: "with other rescuers." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 4, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "The best direction of moisture transfer in the base layer is:", choices: { A: "outward.", B: "from head to feet.", C: "from feet to head.", D: "inward." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 5, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "The best strategy to maintain warmth in the cold winter months is to wear:", choices: { A: "clothing in one layer; multiple-purpose outerwear.", B: "clothing in two layers; a base to retain heat and a water and wind-repelling outer layer.", C: "clothing in three layers; a base to retain heat, a middle insulating layer, and a water and windrepelling outer layer.", D: "clothing primarily made of cotton." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 6, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "Which of the following SPF ratings would provide the greatest level of protection?", choices: { A: "6", B: "15", C: "30", D: "50" }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 7, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "Some vector-borne illnesses are transmitted to humans via:", choices: { A: "eating partially cooked foods.", B: "deer ticks.", C: "contact with human feces.", D: "sneezing and coughing." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 8, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "Wearing clean gloves, an impervious gown, and goggles while cleaning a long-board contaminated with blood helps protect the OEC technician from which form of potential infectious disease transmission?", choices: { A: "Airborne", B: "Indirect contact with an object contaminated with pathogens", C: "Ingestion", D: "Direct contact with a human with infectious pathogens" }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 9, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "Pathogens from a scene can harm rescuers if they:", choices: { A: "invade the body.", B: "pass between victims.", C: "escape the scene.", D: "are UV-durable." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 10, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "The practice of protecting yourself from exposure to body fluids based on the assumption that all patients are potentially infectious is referred to as:", choices: { A: "standard precautions.", B: "exposure control.", C: "personal protective equipment.", D: "body fluid precautions." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 11, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "Which one of the following techniques is one of the most effective techniques that OEC technicians can use to prevent the spread of infection?", choices: { A: "Disinfecting their equipment", B: "Wearing gloves", C: "Washing their hands", D: "Getting immunizations" }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 12, sectionId: 3, sectionName: "Rescuer Safety", text: "When caring for a patient who was stabbed with a knife in the ski area's bar (a crime scene situation), it is important for the OEC technician to do all of the following to support \"chain of custody\" except:", choices: { A: "do not remove, move, or otherwise disturb anything in the environment, except as is absolutely necessary to provide critical care to patient.", B: "wrap the knife found on the floor next to the patient in plastic and hand it to the EMTs so they can show the length of the knife to the Emergency Department staff.", C: "notify law enforcement immediately.", D: "let law enforcement personnel handle any materials that could be used as evidence." }, answer: "B" },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: 4,
    name: "ICS & MCI",
    questionCount: 25,
    questions: [
      { num: 1, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "Which one of the following statements about the Incident Command System is true?", choices: { A: "Each EMS agency can use its own codes and terms.", B: "There is a separate commander for EMS, fire, and law enforcement personnel.", C: "Each individual responder is accountable to two supervisors.", D: "ICS operates with standardized terminology to avoid confusion." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 2, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "Of the five functional areas within the Incident Command System (ICS) structure, the first to be established should be:", choices: { A: "operations section.", B: "incident command.", C: "planning section.", D: "logistics section." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 3, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "The primary function of the incident commander is to:", choices: { A: "not expand command to any other agency", B: "provide overall leadership at an incident.", C: "obtain supplies needed to care for all patients.", D: "ensure that radio communications are established." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 4, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "The incident commander has assigned you to be the operations section chief. In this role, you are responsible for all of the following except:", choices: { A: "reducing immediate hazards.", B: "restoring the scene to normalcy.", C: "participating in the planning process.", D: "determining incident objectives and strategy." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 5, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "Which of the following tasks is not a responsibility of the incident commander?", choices: { A: "Triaging the injured patients", B: "Establishing the incident command post", C: "Determining incident objectives and strategies", D: "Providing overall management of the incident" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 6, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "All of the following are functional areas of the incident command system structure except:", choices: { A: "planning section.", B: "operations section.", C: "transportation section.", D: "finance/administration section." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 7, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "In the incident command system, the operations section is responsible for:", choices: { A: "collecting, assessing, and distributing incidentrelated data.", B: "executing the strategy of the incident action plan.", C: "providing financial management.", D: "providing support for all functional areas." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 8, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "A formal, organized method for managing an incident, regardless of its cause, size, scope, or complexity, is called:", choices: { A: "a multi-agency coordination system.", B: "a federal incident management system.", C: "an incident command system.", D: "an emergency strike team." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 9, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "In the incident command system, which of the following sections is responsible for maintaining all incident reports except for financials?", choices: { A: "Logistics section", B: "Operations section", C: "Records section", D: "Planning section" }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 10, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "The person responsible for maintaining equipment and ensuring that facilities meet specified needs is the:", choices: { A: "operations chief.", B: "logistics chief.", C: "maintenance chief.", D: "planning chief." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 11, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "In the incident command system, the section responsible for maintaining injury, death, and damage documentation as well as maintaining reimbursement records is the:", choices: { A: "planning section.", B: "operations section.", C: "logistics section.", D: "finance/administration section." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 12, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "Which one of the following triage tag indicates the lowest priority for care, \"expectant,\" for a patient at a multiple-casualty incident using the ID-ME triage categories?", choices: { A: "A yellow tag", B: "A red tag", C: "A black/gray tag", D: "A green tag" }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 13, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "You are transporting a patient at a multiplecasualty incident. The patient has a yellow triage tag. This tag means:", choices: { A: "treatment of the patient could be delayed.", B: "the patient has no injuries.", C: "the patient should be with the \"walking wounded.\"", D: "the patient has a head injury with altered mental status." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 14, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "The most widely used triage categorization system in the world is \"ID-ME.\" This acronym represents the four specific triage categories used by NATO forces, National Disaster Life Support, public safety agencies, and search and rescue groups. The ID-ME triage categories are:", choices: { A: "immediate, delayed, maximum, and exceptional.", B: "immediate, delayed, minimal, and expectant.", C: "immediate, detain, minimal, and expectant.", D: "immediate, delayed, minimal, and exceptional." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 15, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "At a multiple-casualty incident that is using the STARTTriage method, you are brought a patient with a red tag tied to his wrist. You should recognize which one of the following?", choices: { A: "Immediate care and transport of the patient are necessary.", B: "Delayed care and transport of the patient are permissible.", C: "The patient has a minor wrist injury.", D: "The patient is deceased." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 16, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "You are at an outside skiing exhibition when a spectator bleacher collapses. Several injured people are walking around with various injuries. Which of the following instructions is most appropriate for these ambulatory patients?", choices: { A: "\"Walk to the area with the medical providers.\"", B: "\"Sit down here so I can do a quick assessment on you.\"", C: "\"Put this yellow tag on your wrist and go to the ticket booth at the bottom of the slope.\"", D: "\"Leave the ski area and go to the hospital. Others are hurt more seriously than you.\"" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 17, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "There is a fight involving approximately 20 bar patrons. Weapons were used, and there are varying degrees and types of injuries. The first person on scene has started assessing a person lying on the floor with blood covering his shirt. Quick assessment reveals him to be breathing at 24 times per minute. Which of the following actions should be done next using the START triage method?", choices: { A: "Assist ventilation with a BVM.", B: "Check for a radial pulse or capillary refill.", C: "Attend to the next patient.", D: "Place a yellow tag on his wrist." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 18, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "At the scene of a multiple-casualty incident, you are presented with a patient who is not breathing. According to the Simple Triage and Rapid Transport (START) system, which of the following actions should you take next?", choices: { A: "Place a red tag on the patient.", B: "Start assisting ventilation with a BVM.", C: "Open the airway.", D: "Place a black tag on the patient." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 19, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "You are triaging using the Simple Triage and Rapid Transport (START) system, and you find a patient who is breathing 18 times per minute and has a radial pulse. Which one of the following actions should you take next?", choices: { A: "Check to see if the patient can follow simple commands.", B: "Check the patient's blood pressure.", C: "Move the patient to the treatment area.", D: "Place a yellow tag on the patient." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 20, sectionId: 4, sectionName: "ICS & MCI", text: "In using the Simple Triage and Rapid Transport (START) system of triage, which one of the following patients should have a yellow tag applied before being moved to the treatment area?", choices: { A: "A male with a respiratory rate of 8, no radial pulse, and unresponsive mental status", B: "A female with a leg fracture who has a respiratory rate of 22, and a palpable radial pulse and who squeezes your fingers when instructed to do so", C: "A female with gasping respirations, no radial pulse, and unresponsive mental status", D: "A male with a respiratory rate of 40 and a palpable radial pulse who squeezes your fingers when instructed to do so" }, answer: "B" },

      { num: 16, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Mechanical tattooing is defined as:", choices: { A: "a form of body art in which dye is injected under the skin.", B: "a type of self-mutilation requiring psychiatric follow-up for the patient.", C: "the introduction of foreign debris such as dirt, gunpowder, or small rocks into the skin.", D: "multiple punctures made by a nail gun." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 17, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Thermal burns caused by the skin directly contacting hot water or hot steam:", choices: { A: "are the least common type of burn.", B: "are the most common type of burn.", C: "result from tanning beds.", D: "result from exposure to Gamma radiation." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 18, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following substances cause the most serious chemical burns?", choices: { A: "An acid with a pH of 1", B: "A chemical with a pH of 7", C: "An alkaline chemical or base with a pH of 8", D: "An acid with a pH of 6" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 19, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Exposure to direct or alternating electrical current produces severe external and internal burn injuries because:", choices: { A: "the skin is a poor conductor with a high resistance, and blood vessels are good conductors with low resistance.", B: "both the skin and blood vessels are good conductors with low resistance.", C: "the skin is a good conductor with a high resistance, and blood vessels are good conductors with low resistance.", D: "skin is a poor conductor with a low resistance, and blood vessels are good conductors with low resistance." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 20, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "When managing electrical burns, OEC technicians should always:", choices: { A: "use moist dressings.", B: "use antibiotic ointments.", C: "assess for signs and symptoms of internal injuries.", D: "use a topical ointment on the skin." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 21, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements concerning a patient who received electrical burns to his hand after grabbing a live wire is true?", choices: { A: "The burning will continue for hours, perhaps days.", B: "The patient will remain an electrocution hazard to rescuers for several minutes after being removed from the source of electricity.", C: "The extent of tissue damage may be much greater than it appears on the surface.", D: "Electrical burns are a minor injury." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 22, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "In a hospital accident, what might cause radiation burns?", choices: { A: "X-ray machine", B: "Steam pipes", C: "Spilled soup", D: "Exposed wires" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 23, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Severe external bleeding should be controlled during what phase of a patient assessment?", choices: { A: "The primary assessment", B: "The scene size-up", C: "The rapid secondary survey", D: "The reassessment" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 24, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "When managing a patient with soft-tissue injuries, it is essential that you:", choices: { A: "thoroughly clean all lacerations.", B: "control any bleeding with sterile dressings only.", C: "use the appropriate personal protective equipment.", D: "cover any hematomas with an occlusive dressing." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 25, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following sentences best describes a partial- thickness burn?", choices: { A: "The skin is red and moist, and blisters have formed.", B: "The skin is charred or blackened and lacks sensation.", C: "The skin is red but dry, no blisters formed, and painful.", D: "The skin is white and dry with no sensation of pain." }, answer: "A" },

      { num: 29, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Hoarseness or voice changes in a burn patient should alert an OEC technician that the:", choices: { A: "patient may be extremely anxious about the injury.", B: "patient most likely is experiencing an inhalation injury causing swelling to the airway, a true emergency.", C: "patient should be treated as a pediatric patient.", D: "patient has altered mental status." }, answer: "B" },

      { num: 35, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements about pressure dressings and bandages is true?", choices: { A: "All pressure dressings must be airtight to prevent contamination.", B: "Bandages should be applied in a distal-toproximal manner.", C: "Dressings are placed over bandages.", D: "Gauze should be placed in an open wound before a pressure dressing is applied." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 36, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "For which of the following injuries may elevation be used to control bleeding?", choices: { A: "For a laceration to the forearm", B: "For no injuries, as elevation has not been shown to help control bleeding", C: "For an abrasion on the lower leg", D: "For a puncture wound to the foot" }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 37, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following actions should you take next when direct pressure and packing the wound have failed to control arterial bleeding on a patient's lower leg?", choices: { A: "Provide oxygen at 15 LPM with a nonrebreather mask.", B: "Apply a tourniquet below the knee.", C: "Immediately transport the patient by ambulance.", D: "Apply a tourniquet above the knee and splint the extremity." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 38, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements indicates that the speaker understands the application of a tourniquet?", choices: { A: "\"A tourniquet should be applied tightly enough so that arterial blood flow distal to the tourniquet is completely stopped.\"", B: "\"If the tourniquet appears to have stopped the bleeding, you should loosen it slightly to allow a small amount of blood to perfuse the tissues.\"", C: "\"Arteries run close to the body's surface in a joint, so the best place to apply a tourniquet is over the joint just above the artery.\"", D: "\"A tourniquet should be applied only when directed by medical control.\"" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 39, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements about the use of a tourniquet is true?", choices: { A: "It should be placed as distal as possible but at least several inches proximal to the wound.", B: "It can be used on most any part of the body except the neck.", C: "On an arm or leg, it should be placed 1 inch from either the elbow or knee.", D: "Tourniquets are a first resort and should be used frequently." }, answer: "A" },

      { num: 42, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements indicates that the speaker understands bandaging?", choices: { A: "\"Bandages are sterile gauze pads used to stop bleeding.\"", B: "\"Bandaging material is used to secure a dressing in place.\"", C: "\"Bandaging material must always be sterile.\"", D: "\"After you apply a bandage, a dressing should always be put over it.\"" }, answer: "B" },

      { num: 44, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements indicates that the speaker understands dressing and bandaging a wound?", choices: { A: "\"When applying a bandage over a dressing, apply it very tightly so the bandage won't fall off.\"", B: "\"If bleeding from a wound cannot be stopped initially with direct pressure, apply a bandage so you can take care of other injuries.\"", C: "\"Leave the tips of the fingers or toes exposed when bandaging an arm or a leg so you can continue to assess CMS.\"", D: "\"Place a bandage across the joint proximal to the wound because this helps control bleeding by applying pressure to the underlying blood vessels.\"" }, answer: "C" },

      { num: 49, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements about amputations is true?", choices: { A: "Keep the amputated part at body temperature when sending it to the hospital with the patient.", B: "A badly mangled or damaged amputated part should not be preserved or sent to the hospital because it cannot be reattached.", C: "Surgeons can reattach an amputated part only if it has been without a blood supply for less than one hour.", D: "All amputated body parts should be preserved and sent to the hospital with the patient." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 50, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements about impaled objects not affecting the airway is true?", choices: { A: "Allow only the patient to pull the impaled object out because that will hurt less.", B: "The impaled object should be left in place during transport.", C: "A wound made by an impaled object always bleeds profusely.", D: "An impaled object never causes serious underlying tissue damage." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 51, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements about a highpressure injection injury is false?", choices: { A: "The presenting wound is typically large.", B: "The injury involves the introduction of a liquid or gas into the body from a pressurized source.", C: "The injury may require surgical amputation of the injured part.", D: "The injury typically involves the limbs." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 52, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Which of the following statements about an impaled object is true?", choices: { A: "The primary treatment goal in the field is to stabilize the object in the position found.", B: "The primary treatment in the field is to remove the object without causing further bleeding or causing as little bleeding as possible.", C: "OEC technicians may remove only objects that are impaled in an extremity.", D: "OEC technicians may remove objects that are impaled in the chest or abdomen." }, answer: "A" },

      { num: 54, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "For the OEC technician, the first priority in managing a patient with a thermal burn is:", choices: { A: "assessing for airway compromise.", B: "completing a secondary survey.", C: "stopping the burning process to prevent further injury.", D: "applying dry sterile dressings." }, answer: "C" },

      { num: 56, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "In treating a burn patient, you should cool and irrigate the burned tissue with:", choices: { A: "room-temperature tap water", B: "chilled tap water for 5 minutes.", C: "tap water warmed to 102°F for 15 minutes.", D: "tap water warmed to 95°F for 10 minutes." }, answer: "A" },

      { num: 58, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "Chemical burns result from exposure to:", choices: { A: "ultraviolet light.", B: "steam.", C: "hot light bulbs.", D: "caustic substances." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 59, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "For the OEC technician, the first priority in managing a patient with an electrical burn is:", choices: { A: "assessing for airway compromise.", B: "assessing for potential c-spine injury.", C: "ensuring the power source has been turned off.", D: "ensuring you have an AED available if needed." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 60, sectionId: 19, sectionName: "Soft Tissue & Burns", text: "When treating a patient burned by a dry chemical, it is important to brush away any dry residue before flushing with water because:", choices: { A: "flushing will expose other areas around the burn.", B: "some dry chemicals are activated by water.", C: "a containment area needs to be set up to catch the runoff water.", D: "flushing will cause the skin's pores to open." }, answer: "B" },

      { num: 17, sectionId: 20, sectionName: "Musculoskeletal", text: "Which of the following statements indicates that an OEC technician has a good understanding of what a joint dislocation is?", choices: { A: "\"If a joint is dislocated, the patient can move it without pain.\"", B: "\"A dislocation is a separation or displacement of the bones of a joint.\"", C: "\"A distal pulse is absent only in the case of a fracture.\"", D: "\"Patients with a joint dislocation experience very little pain.\"" }, answer: "B" },

      { num: 16, sectionId: 30, sectionName: "Pediatrics", text: "The increased pliability of the ribs of children makes them more prone to:", choices: { A: "bruising of the lung.", B: "rib fractures.", C: "cardiac arrest.", D: "over inflation of the lungs." }, answer: "A" },

      { num: 18, sectionId: 30, sectionName: "Pediatrics", text: "Bilateral injuries, circumferential bruising, and pattern bruises are suggestive of:", choices: { A: "shaken child syndrome.", B: "child abuse.", C: "suicidal behavior.", D: "infant neglect." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 19, sectionId: 30, sectionName: "Pediatrics", text: "When assessing a 3-year-old child for possible injuries after the mother's boyfriend said the child fell down a flight of stairs, which of the following findings would raise your suspicion that the child may be a victim of physical abuse?", choices: { A: "The child cries when you palpate his arm.", B: "Several bruises are located on the child's knees and shins.", C: "The child has a broken clavicle.", D: "Circumferential bruising is apparent on the child's arm." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 20, sectionId: 30, sectionName: "Pediatrics", text: "Which of the following statements is most appropriate concerning dealing with caregivers and children during a medical emergency?", choices: { A: "\"I try to include caregivers in all that I do with their child so that the child and the caregivers are more comfortable.\"", B: "\"It is best to separate caregivers from the child so that proper assessment and care can be given.\"", C: "\"I include caregivers in the care until I get the information I need; then I remove the child and continue the assessment in the first-aid room.\"", D: "\"I tell caregivers that everything will be okay so that they are calm, and I am better able to help their child.\"" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 21, sectionId: 30, sectionName: "Pediatrics", text: "The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends the use of the Pediatric Triangle to quickly determine if a child is \"sick or not sick.\" This method allows rescuers to quickly assess all of the following about the patient except his/her:", choices: { A: "circulation.", B: "breathing.", C: "history of illness or injury.", D: "appearance." }, answer: "C" },

      { num: 29, sectionId: 30, sectionName: "Pediatrics", text: "When assessing a 3-year-old child with a respiratory illness, which of the following assessment findings would be least concerning to you?", choices: { A: "Retractions observed above the clavicles", B: "Paradoxical breathing", C: "Patient in the tripod position", D: "A respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute" }, answer: "D" },

      { num: 3, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "The son of an 88- year-old patient states that he told his mother to increase the amount of an antibiotic she was taking so she would \"feel better faster.\" This represents a problem because the elderly have:", choices: { A: "decreased respiratory function.", B: "an increased risk for stroke.", C: "decreased liver and kidney function.", D: "an increased risk for cancer." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 4, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "By age 85, the brain of a typical geriatric patient can shrink by as much as 10 percent due to:", choices: { A: "reduced use in learning.", B: "a decrease in brain cell numbers.", C: "reduced fluid volume.", D: "stroke activity." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 5, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "In a typical geriatric patient, a reduction in cerebral blood flow can:", choices: { A: "reduce the amount of glucose and oxygen that reaches the brain.", B: "increase the patient's pulse rate.", C: "decrease the patient's blood pressure.", D: "increase the patient's respiratory rate." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 6, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Which of the following statements shows that an OEC technician has an accurate understanding of vital signs in relation to geriatric patients?", choices: { A: "\"The typical resting heart rate in geriatric patients is less than 60 beats per minute.\"", B: "\"Fever tends to be more common and more severe in elderly patients.\"", C: "\"There is no difference between the vital signs of a geriatric patient and those of a young adult.\"", D: "\"Respiratory capacity is greatly reduced in geriatric patients.\"" }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 7, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "For many geriatric patients, food is less appealing because:", choices: { A: "they engage in less physical activity.", B: "they sleep more and eat less.", C: "their sense of smell is reduced, and they have fewer taste buds.", D: "they have less money for purchasing appealing food." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 8, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "The lung capacity in a healthy 90-year-old patient is ________ that of a 30-year-old patient.", choices: { A: "equal to", B: "three-quarters of", C: "one-quarter of", D: "half of" }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 9, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Some elderly patients have osteoporosis, a condition that results in:", choices: { A: "decreased bone density.", B: "decreased renal output.", C: "decreased insulin production.", D: "gall stone production." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 10, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "For the same individual, on average, blood pressure at age 30 compared to blood pressure to age 70 will be:", choices: { A: "higher.", B: "lower.", C: "the same.", D: "unrelated." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 11, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "In geriatric patients, strokes can be caused by a blockage or by:", choices: { A: "a buildup of dopamine.", B: "a buildup of epinephrine.", C: "a rupture of a cerebral blood vessel.", D: "trauma to the cortex." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 12, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Family members tell you that three hours ago, their 76- year-old mother suddenly became confused and had great difficulty speaking.       { num: 13, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Which of these is a common cause of COPD?", choices: { A: "Atherosclerosis", B: "Chronic bronchitis", C: "Eczema", D: "Allergies" }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 14, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Over 60% of abdominal pain problems in geriatric patients require:", choices: { A: "a trip to the emergency department.", B: "a prescription for a narcotic drug.", C: "surgical intervention.", D: "evaluation for hernia." }, answer: "C" },
      { num: 15, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Many elderly patients participate in a practice called \"polypharmacy,\" which is the:", choices: { A: "use of mail-order pharmacies.", B: "simultaneous taking of multiple medications.", C: "use of generic drugs.", D: "use of designer drugs." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 16, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "To identify all the drugs, prescriptions, herbal supplements, and over-the-counter drugs that a patient may be taking in combination, OEC technicians should use:", choices: { A: "SAMPLE.", B: "OPQRST.", C: "DCAP-BTLS.", D: "AEIOU." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 17, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "The class of medications that is most commonly prescribed to elderly patients is:", choices: { A: "gastrointestinal medications.", B: "respiratory medications.", C: "neurological medications.", D: "cardiovascular medications." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 18, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "One group of drugs prescribed for geriatric patients is beta- blockers.       { num: 19, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Geriatric patients may also have a prescription for a diuretic such as HCTZ or Lasix.       { num: 20, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "The vital signs of elderly patients with excessive internal or external bleeding may not provide an indication of shock:", choices: { A: "if these patients are taking beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers.", B: "because the hearts of elderly patients pump less due to inactivity.", C: "because elderly patients have the ability to compensate for bleeding.", D: "if these patients are taking blood thinners." }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 21, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Compared to younger patients, trauma in geriatric patients results in:", choices: { A: "less-serious injuries due to the slower pace in older patients.", B: "a higher mortality rate.", C: "more bleeding.", D: "more fractures of the extremities." }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 22, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Correcting a life-threatening condition such as external bleeding in elderly patients can be more problematic because:", choices: { A: "the skin of elderly patients does not rebound as quickly as it does in younger patients.", B: "the veins of elderly patients have weaker walls than those in younger patients.", C: "elderly patients may be on Lasix.", D: "many elder patients are taking warfarin or other blood thinners." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 23, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Which of the following statements about traumatic injuries in the elderly is true?", choices: { A: "Motor-vehicle collisions are responsible for over 75 percent of deaths.", B: "Head injuries are easier to detect in the elderly than in younger adults.", C: "Hyperthermia is an early sign of trauma.", D: "Injuries are most commonly caused by falls." }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 24, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Falls result in ____% of all deaths in the geriatric population.", choices: { A: "5", B: "12", C: "40", D: "72" }, answer: "B" },
      { num: 25, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Which of the following conditions must OEC technicians consider when evaluating hypotensive geriatric patients with altered mental status who show no signs of external bleeding, chest injury, or abdominal trauma?", choices: { A: "A hip or pelvic fracture", B: "A tib/fib fracture", C: "A genetic hypotensive condition", D: "Dehydration" }, answer: "A" },
      { num: 26, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "An elderly woman has fallen down three steps and is complaining of back pain.       { num: 27, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Compared to younger individuals, geriatric patients who fall have a higher incidence of fractures to the _____ region of the spine.", choices: { A: "C4-C5", B: "T1-T2", C: "L1-L2", D: "C1-C2" }, answer: "D" },
      { num: 28, sectionId: 31, sectionName: "Geriatrics", text: "Which of the following statements concerning insulin pumps is false?", choices: { A: "They have an external on/off button.", B: "They are implanted in the patient's chest.", C: "They supply insulin via a catheter.", D: "They are commonly found on a patient's belt." }, answer: "B" },
